Kevin / Sofia —

Thanks for the quick review of the MSA & order form redlines. We reviewed the procurement team's comments and our legal team has pushed a few clarifications that will impact how invoices flow and which entity is responsible for tax withholding. High-level items we need to resolve before we can finalize: 

- Invoice recipient: current redline routes all invoices to Acme Health (UK) but our accounting needs to confirm whether you want invoices to go to the purchasing entity (Acme Health Ltd) or the group finance mailbox. This matters for VAT/residency.
- Net terms: the order form currently shows Net45. Procurement asked for Net60 in the EU entity. Legal prefers keeping Net45 with a limited Net60 carve-out for public-sector entities — we need to agree which path.
- Minimum commit / pricing schedule: redline preserved the tiered slab pricing but added a carve-out for burst usage. We need a short doc showing expected monthly token profile per entity to validate the billing ladder.
- Tax / withholding: there is a request that Acme deduct withholding tax at payment. We need to confirm whether Redwood should gross-up or accept net receipts and provide a tax certificate.

I attached our annotated order form (OrderForm_Redline_v2.pdf) and a light invoice mapping proposal in the Drive link. Can you confirm: (1) the invoice recipient entity for legal/PO purposes, (2) which net terms you expect per entity, and (3) whether Acme will provide withholding certificates or prefers Redwood to invoice gross with reverse-charge handling?

If it helps, Ben from sales and Laura from legal are looped to propose operational mappings. Ideally we resolve this in the next 48 hours so we can hand to contracts for signature.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary and the annotated order form. Quick answers from procurement/finance side: 

1) Invoice recipient: For commercial contracts, invoicing should go to Acme Health Ltd (UK entity) and copy group-finance@acmehealth.com. That matches our PO routing and VAT registration.
2) Net terms: we generally operate Net60 for new vendors in EMEA. For this specific deal we can accept Net45 only if Redwood agrees to provide tax residency evidence (certificate of tax residency) and a VAT invoice that supports reverse-charge where applicable. Otherwise procurement will request Net60.
3) Withholding: we do not plan to deduct withholding for services that are subject to reverse-charge. If a payment requires withholding by local law, we will deduct and provide the withholding certificate.

A couple of asks back to you: can Redwood (a) provide a simple per-entity revenue allocation table for the order form so our accounting can map to the correct ledgers, and (b) confirm whether Redwood can sign a clause that invoices are issued net but Redwood will provide tax evidence for VAT/reverse-charge?

If you can send a revised invoice mapping sheet and a short note from legal on the residency/VAT approach, I'll route to our legal and finance. We plan to have procurement sign off by COB Monday if everything is clear.

Best,
Kevin Morris
Head of Procurement — Acme Health

Kevin —

Thanks for the quick visibility. To accelerate, here's what Redwood proposes operationally (short and pragmatic):

- Invoice mapping: Redwood will split invoicing per contracting entity. In this case we will issue invoices to \"Acme Health Ltd (UK)\" and copy group-finance. We will also produce a monthly allocation CSV (token/usage by region/entity) to help your ledger mapping. Attached is a draft invoice_mapping_proposal.xlsx (two tabs: entity_map, monthly_alloc_example).

- Net terms: Redwood prefers to preserve Net45 as standard. However, given your EMEA policy, we're prepared to accept Net60 for invoices issued to EU entities if (1) Acme confirms in writing that reverse-charge applies where law permits, and (2) Acme provides a PO/confirmation referencing the order form. If Acme cannot confirm reverse-charge, Redwood requests Net45 and will provide tax residency and VAT evidence.

- Withholding: Redwood will not gross-up. If withholding is applied by Acme, we ask for the withholding certificate and we will issue a credit/adjustment where applicable. 

- Documentation: Laura (cc'd) will provide a 1-paragraph legal note describing the residency/VAT stance that you can attach to the procurement packet.

If that matches your expectations I'll have legal draft the short clause and update the order form to show invoice recipient and per-entity net terms. 

Kimberly — can you confirm we'll get the PO by Monday and whether Sofia / group-finance prefer a consolidated monthly invoice or entity-by-entity invoices?

Cheers,
